season_storylines: Ten teams open 2026 with new head coaches - John Harbaugh (NYG), Mike McCarthy (PIT), Kevin Stefanski (ATL), Robert Saleh with OC Brian Daboll (TEN), Jesse Minter (BAL), Joe Brady (BUF), Todd Monken (CLE), Klint Kubiak (LV), Jeff Hafley (MIA), Mike LaFleur (ARI) - so roughly a third of the league has scheme and pace turnover that resets pass rates, red-zone tendencies and every incumbent's role.

Patrick Mahomes is coming off a Week 15 2025 ACL tear and KC signed Kenneth Walker III to a 3-year $43M deal, so his 2025 rushing production (64 carries, 5 rush TDs) should shrink and his 6-pt-TD ceiling is priced above his likely output - he is no longer an automatic top-5 QB.

Matthew Stafford won 2025 MVP at 4,707 yards and 46 TDs with a 7.7% TD rate, and the Rams carry a league-high 11.5 win total, so the whole LAR pass game is priced at its absolute peak entering his age-38 season - TD regression hits him and his receivers hardest in a 6-pt passing TD format.

Five unresolved QB battles (ATL Penix vs Tua, MIN J.J. McCarthy vs Kyler Murray, CLE Watson vs Shedeur Sanders, LV No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza vs Kirk Cousins, ARI Brissett vs Minshew vs rookie Carson Beck) hold the value of every skill player on those five offenses hostage until winners are named.

Malik Nabers' ACL rehab hit scar-tissue complications requiring a second procedure and he is headed toward PUP with a possible Week 5-6 return, so an early-round WR price now buys a month of zeros against a Week 1 date with Dallas.

Josh Jacobs was arrested this offseason on charges including domestic abuse and strangulation with the case still open, and the baseline league discipline for a first violation is six games, so his ADP carries hidden suspension risk while MarShawn Lloyd is a near-free hedge in Green Bay.

Rashee Rice served 30 days in jail in May 2026 for a probation violation on top of his 2025 six-game suspension and is coming off knee surgery recovery with additional NFL discipline still possible, making him one of the most fragile mid-round WR prices on the board.

The 49ers' pass-catching room is in flux all at once - George Kittle is racing an Achilles tear (torn January 2026) to be ready Week 1, Ricky Pearsall may need season-ending PCL surgery, Brandon Aiyuk's status is clouded by repeated public outbursts, and veterans Christian Kirk (calf) and Deebo Samuel were added (verify) - so Purdy's target tree is unusually unsettled for a 10.5-win team.

The betting market has reigning champion Seattle at 10.5 wins with a rookie-led backfield, New England at 10.5 off its Super Bowl run, and Arizona and Miami in the basement at 4.5 - game-script projections favor NE and SEA volume and make ARI/MIA passing games negative-script traps.

Rookie roles are unusually fantasy-ready: Fernando Mendoza went No. 1 overall to Kubiak's Raiders, RB Jeremiyah Love went No. 3 to Arizona into a wide-open backfield, WR Carnell Tate is Tennessee's most pro-ready target, and Jadarian Price opens as Seattle's lead back with Zach Charbonnet (ACL) out until midseason.

teams.outlook: New HC Mike LaFleur inherits a 4.5-win-total rebuild with a three-way Brissett/Minshew/Carson Beck QB battle, so No. 3 overall pick Jeremiyah Love's projected volume-plus-TD role is the only premium asset here while Trey McBride's catch-volume profile loses value in non-PPR.

Kevin Stefanski takes over a 6.5-win team where Michael Penix Jr. is not yet cleared from his ACL and Tua Tagovailoa already had a back flare-up in camp, so the run game and Bijan Robinson's TD equity are the only stable investments until the QB settles.

Jesse Minter replaces John Harbaugh but Lamar Jackson's rushing floor keeps him elite in this format, while Derrick Henry's age-and-workload cliff and Keaton Mitchell's burst make the backfield a fade-the-price, buy-the-backup situation on a co-league-high 11.5 win total.
Promoted OC Joe Brady now runs the whole show and the offense added DJ Moore, keeping Josh Allen the format's premier asset (rushing TDs plus 6-pt passing TDs) on a 10.5 win total.

WR Chris Brazzell II's knee injury ended his season and pushes targets to Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette, while Jonathon Brooks is finally cleared and praised by Dave Canales as a three-down back - a direct TD-role threat to Chuba Hubbard's workload.

Year 2 of Ben Johnson calling plays for Caleb Williams comes with roughly 150 vacated targets after DJ Moore and Olamide Zaccheaus departed and Rome Odunze rehabbing foot surgery, setting up Luther Burden III for a high-yardage breakout on a 9.5 win total.

Continuity offense around Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins with a mid-pack 9.5 win total (verify camp health); the notable camp injury, rookie EDGE Shemar Stewart's leg, is a defense-only story.

New HC Todd Monken has no draft-capital loyalty in the Deshaun Watson vs Shedeur Sanders battle after Sanders' Pro Bowl-caliber rookie year, and Harold Fannin Jr. faces TD-and-target regression even with David Njoku gone, all on a 6.5 win total.

Year 2 under Brian Schottenheimer projects near the top of the league in passing yards and TDs, making thin-backfield RB Jaydon Blue (only Phil Mafah behind him) and WR3 Ryan Flournoy cheap TD-equity buys on a 9.5 win total.
Bo Nix is being flagged as scheme-dependent (needs favorable third-down situations) despite a 9.5 win total, so pay for the defense/DST tiers here rather than the pass game's TD upside.
Still a 10.5-win contender with a run-heavy, red-zone-efficient identity, but Sam LaPorta is a consensus fade at his price as the TD share spreads across the roster.

Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks left 131 targets behind for Christian Watson (deep-threat profile ideal for non-PPR if healthy), Jayden Reed and 2025 first-rounder Matthew Golden, while Josh Jacobs carries open-case suspension risk that makes MarShawn Lloyd a priority handcuff.

Houston rebuilt the O-line and added David Montgomery to fix C.J. Stroud's support, and with Christian Kirk gone and Tank Dell still rehabbing, big-bodied Jayden Higgins is the red-zone breakout behind Nico Collins on a 9.5 win total.

Daniel Jones returns off a career 2025 season but Michael Pittman Jr. departed (verify) and Alec Pierce (ankle surgery) may not be full-go until Week 1, so the 7.5-win passing game is thin on proven yardage producers.

Travis Etienne is gone and Liam Coen's backfield is Bhayshul Tuten's to win (7 TDs on 93 touches, elite missed-tackle rate) with Chris Rodriguez Jr. off foot surgery threatening early-down work, while Travis Hunter's two-way role keeps his snap count a gamble.

Mahomes' post-ACL season plus the Kenneth Walker III signing points to fewer QB rushing points and more handoffs, and Rashee Rice's legal/discipline overhang makes the pass game's mid-round prices riskier than the 10.5 win total suggests.

Mike McDaniel now runs the offense (verify role) around a healthy line, and Omarion Hampton - who flashed RB1 play before his 2025 ankle fracture - is the breakout centerpiece with Ladd McConkey and a rebounding Quentin Johnston as the top targets on a 9.5 win total.

A league-high 11.5 win total is priced on Stafford repeating an age-38 MVP season (46 TDs, 7.7% TD rate), which is the classic setup to pay peak price for regressing TD totals - though rookie TE Terrance Ferguson emerging as the de facto WR3 is a cheap way in.

Klint Kubiak inherits No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza vs Kirk Cousins plus Ashton Jeanty and Brock Bowers, and even at a 5.5 win total Jeanty's Year 2 leap is live because his 1.26 yards before contact per carry (worst among qualifying backs) blames the departed scheme and blocking, not him.

Defensive-minded Jeff Hafley takes over a torn-down 4.5-win roster whose top three receivers have fewer than 130 combined career catches, so Jaylen Waddle's efficiency profile is capped by volume-poor, negative-script projections.

Kevin O'Connell is running a true open competition between J.J. McCarthy and Kyler Murray, and until it resolves Justin Jefferson's ceiling and the 8.5 win total both hinge on it - Murray winning would also add a rushing-QB fantasy asset.

Off a Super Bowl run with a 10.5 win total, the fantasy question is whether TreVeyon Henderson turns Rhamondre Stevenson's lead job into a timeshare - the goal-line split decides which back matters in this format - while Drake Maye's price now assumes another leap.

Tyler Shough closed his rookie year with six straight 17-plus-point games and a 22.2% goal-line carry share, and the Saints added Travis Etienne and rookie WR Jordyn Tyson while extending Chris Olave this week - a sneaky 6-pt-passing-TD value stack at a 7.5 win total.

John Harbaugh now coaches the Giants with Jaxson Dart entering Year 2, but Malik Nabers' scar-tissue setback (possible Week 5-6 return) and an unsettled Isaiah Likely vs Theo Johnson TE timeshare make every pass-catcher here a discount-or-avoid on a 7.5 win total.

Geno Smith projects for mediocre passing volume (bottom-third yards and TDs) at a 5.5 win total, but a fully healthy Garrett Wilson and downfield-buzz WR2 Adonai Mitchell fit the deep-threat-over-slot value model, while rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq is buried behind Mason Taylor.

A 10.5-win contender whose formula - Jalen Hurts' rushing TDs and Saquon Barkley's goal-line monopoly - is exactly what this format pays for, with rookie WR Makai Lemon (hamstring resolved) only a gradual-role stash.

Mike McCarthy replaces Mike Tomlin and should throw far more than Arthur Smith did, with Aaron Rodgers still starting and Michael Pittman Jr. and Germie Bernard added (verify), while the Jaylen Warren vs Rico Dowdle committee makes the goal-line winner the only back worth paying for.

The reigning champs (10.5 win total) lost Kenneth Walker III and OC Klint Kubiak, and rookie Jadarian Price opens as the lead back with George Holani on third downs and Zach Charbonnet (ACL) back midseason - Price's early-season TD window is real but has an expiration risk.

A 10.5-win offense with maximum pass-catcher chaos - Kittle racing an Achilles tear for Week 1, Pearsall possibly out for the year, Aiyuk's status in doubt, Kirk hurt and new veterans added (verify) - which concentrates early-season value in Christian McCaffrey even as his 450-touch 2025 workload screams decline risk.

Baker Mayfield's extension deadline passed unsigned and David Blough takes over play-calling, but Mike Evans' departure opens the No. 1 role for Emeka Egbuka's top-10-upside breakout, with Kenneth Gainwell arriving from Pittsburgh to handle passing downs at an 8.5 win total.

Robert Saleh plus OC Brian Daboll is the league's most fantasy-interesting new staff because Cam Ward's Year 2 leap is the thesis, with rookie Carnell Tate, Wan'Dale Robinson and a healthy-again Calvin Ridley fighting to be his go-to on a 6.5 win total.

A 7.5 win total signals real market skepticism about this roster around Jayden Daniels, but his rushing floor is format-proof even if the surrounding pass-game volume disappoints (verify supporting-cast health).

breakout_watch.name: Jeremiyah Love
breakout_watch.why: No. 3 overall pick walking into Arizona's empty backfield; the last nine top-12 drafted RBs all finished top-12, and a bell-cow yardage-plus-goal-line role is the single most valuable archetype in non-PPR.

breakout_watch.name: Omarion Hampton
breakout_watch.why: Posted an RB1-caliber 24.9-point game before his 2025 ankle fracture, now healthy in a McDaniel-influenced Chargers scheme behind a healthy line - power profile means TDs, not checkdowns.

breakout_watch.name: Bhayshul Tuten
breakout_watch.why: Etienne's departure clears the Jacksonville lead role; 7 TDs on just 93 rookie touches and a 31% missed-tackle-forced rate is exactly the TD-per-touch efficiency this scoring rewards.

breakout_watch.name: Ashton Jeanty
breakout_watch.why: Ranked last in yards before contact (1.26) as a rookie, indicting the old Raiders blocking, and Klint Kubiak's run scheme plus an improved offense resets his TD and yardage ceiling.

breakout_watch.name: Jadarian Price
breakout_watch.why: Opens as the reigning champs' lead back with Charbonnet (ACL) out until midseason - a champion offense's goal-line work at a rookie price, though the window may close when Charbonnet returns.

breakout_watch.name: Jaydon Blue
breakout_watch.why: Dallas coaches report night-and-day improvement and only Phil Mafah stands between him and the RB touches in an offense projected near the top of the league in scoring - cheap TD equity.

breakout_watch.name: Emeka Egbuka
breakout_watch.why: Mike Evans' departure hands him the Tampa No. 1 role after four 20-plus-point rookie games; his yardage-and-TD profile, not empty catches, drives the top-10 WR upside.

breakout_watch.name: Luther Burden III
breakout_watch.why: 150 vacated Bears targets (DJ Moore, Zaccheaus gone), Odunze rehabbing foot surgery, and a 2.92 rookie yards-per-route-run in Ben Johnson's offense - elite yards-after-catch means real yardage points, not slot volume.

breakout_watch.name: Jayden Higgins
breakout_watch.why: Third on Houston in targets as a rookie with 6 TDs, and Christian Kirk's exit plus Tank Dell's rehab clear the red-zone WR2 role next to an injury-prone Nico Collins.

breakout_watch.name: Tyler Shough
breakout_watch.why: Six straight games of 17+ points to close 2025 plus a 22.2% goal-line carry share - rushing TDs and 6-pt passing TDs at a free price, now with Etienne and rookie Jordyn Tyson added.

breakout_watch.name: Cam Ward
breakout_watch.why: Brian Daboll built Josh Allen's leap and now coordinates Ward's Year 2 with real weapons added (Tate, Wan'Dale Robinson); a mobile QB in a 6-pt passing TD league is the classic late-round ceiling play.

breakout_watch.name: Adonai Mitchell
breakout_watch.why: Camp reports have him clearly ahead for the Jets' WR2 job, and his downfield profile with Geno Smith fits deep-threat-over-slot-compiler value in zero-PPR.

breakout_watch.name: Christian Watson
breakout_watch.why: Was the WR12 over his last healthy 10-game stretch and inherits part of 131 vacated Packers targets; a pure vertical yardage-and-TD receiver is worth more here than his PPR-based ADP implies.

fade_watch.name: Matthew Stafford
fade_watch.why: Age-38 season after an MVP year built on a 7.7% TD rate and 46 TDs - in a 6-pt passing TD league you would be paying full retail for near-certain TD regression.

fade_watch.name: Patrick Mahomes
fade_watch.why: Coming off a Week 15 ACL tear with KC paying Kenneth Walker III $43M to run more - his rushing points shrink and the offense's TD distribution shifts away from his legs and arm.

fade_watch.name: Derrick Henry
fade_watch.why: Age-and-touches cliff flagged league-wide, and Baltimore's new staff under Jesse Minter has speedy Keaton Mitchell pushing for work - the goal-line share is the last thing to go, but the yardage is already slipping (verify camp usage).

fade_watch.name: Christian McCaffrey
fade_watch.why: Coming off a 450-touch 2025 season, the historical post-mega-workload decline pattern, and SF's injured receiving room may force even more early load onto him - peak price, downside tail.

fade_watch.name: Josh Jacobs
fade_watch.why: Open domestic-violence case with a baseline six-game suspension precedent, declining 4.0 YPC efficiency, 2,109 career touches at age 28 - triple-stacked risk at a starter price.

fade_watch.name: Malik Nabers
fade_watch.why: Second knee procedure for scar tissue, PUP-bound with a possible Week 5-6 return - and his target-hog profile is worth less in zero-PPR even when healthy.

fade_watch.name: Mike Evans
fade_watch.why: Age-33 season off a career-low 12.1 PPG with nine games missed, now in a new uniform (49ers, verify) - only two WRs this century have delivered top-25 seasons at 33-plus.

fade_watch.name: Rashee Rice
fade_watch.why: 30 days of jail time in May for a probation violation, knee surgery recovery, and unresolved potential for further NFL discipline - the range of outcomes includes zero-week stretches.

fade_watch.name: Trey McBride
fade_watch.why: Elite catch totals but chronically low TD conversion on a 4.5-win-total offense with a new staff - a slot-compiler profile is exactly what this league's scoring discounts.

fade_watch.name: Harold Fannin Jr.
fade_watch.why: 2025 production already maxed out expectations, defenses get an offseason to adjust, and Cleveland's unresolved QB battle plus a 6.5 win total cap the TD upside his new price requires.

uncertainty_note: Genuinely unsettled as of July 31: five starting QB battles (ATL, MIN, CLE, LV, ARI) that gate the value of every skill player on those rosters; league discipline outcomes for Josh Jacobs (open case) and Rashee Rice (post-jail); Week 1 availability for Malik Nabers (second knee procedure), George Kittle (Achilles), Michael Penix Jr. (ACL clearance) and Ricky Pearsall (possible season-ending PCL surgery); the 49ers' and Steelers' exact receiver pecking orders after heavy turnover; and Seattle's backfield once Zach Charbonnet returns midseason. Several player-team assignments from aggregated sources are tagged (verify) in this brief - treat those specific claims as directional until confirmed by beat reporting.
